wu: Feelings Charades: Students pick a feeling flashcard, act it out without speaking, and classmates guess 'Are you happy/sad/angry/tired?'
wuAlt: Feelings Bingo: Teacher calls out feelings, students mark them on bingo cards; first to shout 'Bingo!' wins
Feelings Chain: One student says 'I am happy', next says 'He is happy, I am sad', continuing the chain
pres: Teacher shows a story about a boy named Ahmed who feels tired because he played football, sad because his friend left, happy because he ate cake, and angry because his brother broke his toy. Model sentences: 'How are you?' 'I am tired because I played football.' Check understanding with thumbs up/down for each feeling-reason pair.
presAlt: Realia Feelings: Teacher holds up objects (ball, toy, cake, photo) and says 'I am happy because I have a cake', students repeat
Puppet Show: Two puppets ask 'How are you?' and answer with feelings + because, students echo
prac: Feelings Dominoes: Students get dominoes with feelings on one half and reasons on the other; they match them and say the full sentence 'I am [feeling] because [reason]'. Teacher circulates to correct pronunciation.
pracAlt: Feelings Memory Game: Cards with feelings and reasons face down; students flip two, match, and say the sentence; if no match, turn back
Feelings Dice: Roll a feelings die and a reason die, then make a sentence
ls: Listen and Match: Teacher reads sentences like 'I am angry because my book is lost' and students point to the matching picture on their worksheet with 4 feelings and 4 reasons.
re: Feelings Relay: Students line up; teacher calls a feeling, first student runs to the board, writes it, runs back, next student writes a reason; team with fastest correct pair wins.
prod: Feelings Doctor Roleplay: In pairs, one is a doctor, one is a patient. Doctor asks 'How are you?', patient answers with feeling + because, then asks 'Why?', doctor guesses. Props: toy stethoscope, bandages.
rw: Read and Complete: Students read a short paragraph like 'Lila is happy because it is Eid. She is not sad.' Then write 2 sentences: 'I am ___ because ___' and 'I am not ___ because ___'.
st: Story: 'The Feelings Monster' where a monster changes feelings; students act out the feelings. End with 'Goodbye Song' (to the tune of 'Twinkle Twinkle') and high-five line.
g: Students act out feelings, classmates guess
Match feeling cards to reason cards and say sentences
Race to write feeling-reason pairs on the board
Ask and answer about feelings with props
Mark called-out feelings on bingo cards
diff: Fast finishers: Draw a picture of themselves with a feeling and write 3 sentences
Support learners: Use sentence frames 'I am ___ because ___' with word banks
hw: Read the 'How are you?' page in your mini-book and circle 3 new words
Draw 4 faces (happy, sad, angry, tired) and write a sentence for each
Ask 3 family members 'How are you?' and write their answers
tip: Use local context like Eid or Independence Day to make feelings relevant—e.g., 'I am happy because it is Eid'.
